about: Honesty scanner corpus for SmartCiti.X : Trade Craft Academy. Every case is run through loop/honesty.mjs (loop/test.mjs, courses_roadmap/test.mjs) and through courses_roadmap/build.py --scan-fixtures; all three must return the expected verdict. These sentences are test fixtures, not statements about the project.

cases.text: The course is accredited by the State Board.
cases.why: plain claim

cases.text: We partnered with a district last spring.
cases.why: plain partnership claim

cases.text: We are accredited by ACME, not endorsed.
cases.why: positional: the negation comes after the claim, in a new clause

cases.text: No. 4765 is accredited by the state board
cases.why: the abbreviation No. is not a negation

cases.text: the program is |accredited| by the board
cases.why: loose pipes are not a regex alternation

cases.text: Being deployed to a pilot site is planned for 2027.
cases.why: planned after the claim does not excuse it

cases.text: This is not a demo. It is accredited by ACME.
cases.why: a negation in the previous sentence does not excuse a claim

cases.text: This is not a demo; it is accredited by ACME.
cases.why: a semicolon ends the clause

cases.text: Rules: accredited|endorsed. We are endorsed by ACME.
cases.why: a sentence beside a rule table is still a claim

cases.text: See e.g. the welders hall. It is endorsed by the union.
cases.why: the abbreviation e.g. neither merges nor splits sentences wrongly

cases.text: Per Art. 5 the course is certified by the board.
cases.why: Art. is an abbreviation, not a sentence end

cases.text: The pilot is planned, but the course is deployed to two schools.
cases.why: a coordinating but starts a new clause

cases.text: not accredited
cases.why: plain negation

cases.text: No accreditation is claimed.
cases.why: negation precedes the noun form

cases.text: Nothing here is endorsed by any union.
cases.why: negation precedes the claim

cases.text: accredited|endorsed|certified by
cases.why: regex alternation source

cases.text: const CLAIM = /accredited|endorsed|certified by|partnered with/i;
cases.why: regex literal

cases.text: This course is not accredited.
cases.why: negation precedes the claim

cases.text: Nothing here is accredited, deployed to schools or endorsed.
cases.why: one negation covers the list that follows it

cases.text: A partnership is proposed, and being deployed to a pilot site is planned for 2027.
cases.why: proposed precedes the claim in the same clause

cases.text: `accredited by` is a phrase the lint hunts.
cases.why: a code span is quoting, not claiming

cases.text:
Example:
```
The course is accredited by ACME.
```
None of this is endorsed.
cases.why: a fenced block is quoting, not claiming

cases.text: No course is accredited, i.e. no board has reviewed it.
cases.why: i.e. does not end the sentence

cases.text: We aren't endorsed by anyone.
cases.why: n't negation

cases.text:
Nothing in this pack is
accredited by any board.
cases.why: a soft line wrap continues the sentence

cases.text: The academy has accreditation from the State Board.
cases.why: noun form: accreditation

cases.text: The course carries an endorsement from the union.
cases.why: noun form: endorsement

cases.text: Graduates receive certification from the board.
cases.why: noun form: certification from

cases.text: We announced a partnership with the parish schools.
cases.why: noun form: partnership with

cases.text: nothing here carries accreditation
cases.why: negation precedes the noun form

cases.text: No endorsement, certification by any board or partnership with a school exists.
cases.why: one negation covers the noun list that follows it
